title: Keep both sides of a bidirectional relationship in step

blocks.text: The page's first edge case: in a bidirectional relationship, always maintain both sides, with a helper such as
That helper still has gaps. Write `Shop.Category` and `Shop.Product` so that the two sides can never disagree:

items: `category.addProduct(p)` adds `p` to the category's products and sets `p.category()` to it. **Moving a product removes it from its old category**, and **adding the same product twice lists it once**.
`category.removeProduct(p)` takes `p` out and **clears its category** (`p.category()` becomes `null`). Removing a product that is not in the category changes nothing.
`category.products()` returns the products in the order they were added. **It hands out no list that edits the category behind `addProduct`'s back.**

blocks.text: Products are compared by identity (two products with the same name are different products).

cases.says: books.addProduct(dune) puts dune in books.products() and makes dune.category() books.
Adding a product that is in Books to Pens removes it from Books' list.
Adding the same product to the same category twice lists it once.
books.removeProduct(dune) takes dune out of the list and sets dune.category() to null; pens.removeProduct(emma), for a product pens does not hold, leaves emma in books.
A product added to the list products() returned does not join the category; only addProduct links both sides.

concepts: Both sides of a bidirectional relationship are kept in step with a helper method on the owning side.
